_meta.title: Nyama — every recipe you love, finally in one place
_meta.description: The recipes you love are asleep in your Instagram saves, your screenshots and your open tabs. Nyama brings them all into one library: yours.
_meta.ogTitle: Nyama — every recipe you love, finally in one place
_meta.ogDescription: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, a blog, a photo of a cookbook page. You share, Nyama files it. Your recipe library, ready to cook.

hero.h1:
You remember it so well.
You just don't know where it is.
hero.lead: Your best recipes are asleep in your Instagram saves, your screenshots and your open tabs. Nyama brings them all into one place. Yours.
sources.label: Where your recipes come from
pb.p1: Last Tuesday you came across the perfect recipe. Thirty seconds of video, a dish that made you hungry on the spot. You saved it, thinking «that one, I'm making it».
pb.p2: Tonight you scroll your saved posts for eight minutes. You move on to your screenshots. You open three tabs. It's in there somewhere, you know it. You can't find it.
pb.punch:
The problem was never finding recipes.
The problem is finding them again.
how.h2: Three moves, and nothing gets lost
how.lead: Capture, organise, cook. Everything else in Nyama exists to serve those three.
p1.p1: A TikTok video, an Instagram post, a blog that never ends, a photo of a cookbook page, a message your mother sent you. You share it to Nyama, and the recipe comes out clean: ingredients on one side, steps on the other.
p1.p2: You didn't retype a thing. It takes seconds.
p1.li1: From the «Share» button in any app
p1.li2: A photo of a book or a card: the text is read for you
p1.li3: A pasted link, pasted text, or by hand if you prefer
p1.li4: You read it over, fix whatever you like, and save
p2.h3: In three years, it'll still be there.
p2.p1: Every recipe joins your library, with its tags and its collections. You search «lemon chicken», you find it. No feed, no algorithm, none of other people's recipes.
p2.p2: Only yours. Filed the way you file things.
p2.li1: A search that digs through titles and ingredients alike
p2.li2: Recipe books: «quick ones», «for having people over», «what the kids will actually eat»
p2.li3: Filters by mealtime, by time, by mood
p2.li4: Your recipes stay on your phone, readable even with no signal
p3.h3: Hands covered in flour, the screen keeping up.
p3.p1: Cook mode shows one step at a time, large, and the screen doesn't go dark at the worst moment. You tick off ingredients as you go. You never lose your place again.
p3.p2: Cooking goes back to being the good part, not an obstacle course.
p3.li1: One step per screen, in large type
p3.li2: The ingredients for that step right in front of you
p3.li3: The screen stays on for the whole cook
p3.li4: Quantities adjust to how many you're feeding
feat.h2: What turns a library into dinner
feat.lead: A well-filed recipe is good. A week of meals already decided is better.
feat.c1p: Your recipes become a list sorted by aisle, quantities added up. You tick items off one-handed at the shop.
feat.c2p: You drop your meals onto the days ahead. On Tuesday evening you stop opening the fridge hoping for an idea. And when the time comes, the reminder rings at mealtime and opens the recipe.
feat.c7p: You send a link, it opens with nothing to install. If they like it, they add it to their own library in one tap.
feat.c8p: You declare your allergies and your diet once. A recipe containing an allergen is flagged, before you cook it.
feat.c3p: Dairy-free, for six instead of four, a little lighter. The recipe rewrites itself, the original doesn't move. With Nyama Plus.
feat.c4p: What's actually on your plate, estimated for you. No calculator, nothing to retype. With Nyama Plus.
feat.c9p: A widget puts the recipe of the day on your home screen and your lock screen. You touch it, it opens.
feat.c5p: Your recipes live on your phone. In a kitchen with no signal, at your parents', on holiday: they're there.
feat.c6p: When the automatic reading isn't sure of itself, Nyama tells you instead of pretending. Two taps and it's fixed.
not.4: A feed where people post their food
not.5: A place that sells you ingredients
not.6: An app that sells your data
not.final:
Nyama is a personal library.
It's nobody's business but yours.
faq.q1: Does it work with all my sources?
faq.a1: Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and its Shorts, Facebook, Pinterest, cooking sites and blogs, a photo of a cookbook page, pasted text, a note or a message: Nyama reads what's written and files it away. And when the recipe is written nowhere — when it only exists spoken in the video — Nyama listens to it and reconstructs it. If it isn't sure, it tells you rather than inventing.
faq.q2: What if the recipe comes out wrong?
faq.a2: Nyama flags the parts it isn't sure about instead of acting as if nothing happened. You read it over, fix it in two taps, and save. A wrong recipe in your library is worse than a missing one.
faq.q3: Do my recipes go to a server?
faq.a3: Your recipes live on your phone. What does go to a server, and only in those cases, is spelled out in the privacy policy. No selling your data, no advertising.
faq.q4: Do I have to create an account?
faq.a4: It does one thing: it keeps your recipes when a phone breaks or gets replaced. So yes, at the end of the walkthrough — with Apple or Google, in a few seconds, no password to remember. You can delete your account and everything in it from the app, without writing to us.
faq.a5: Not yet. Nyama is starting on iPhone. Android will follow if enough people ask for it.
faq.q6: What happens if I stop Nyama Plus?
faq.a6: You keep every recipe. You simply fall back on the free allowance for whatever you add next: 5 recipes a week, topped up every Monday. Nothing is deleted.
cta.h2: Tonight, you know where it is.
cta.lead: File your first recipe in two minutes. The one you set aside and never made: start with that one.
